SMTO-EXE-0106 — The Gateway's web browser tools aren't installed correctly

GUID: 2ef08d82-cd4c-5481-820e-6aee45e86e08
Slug: browser-backend-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work on a computer) couldn't load the software it needs to open a web browser, so this browsing step couldn't open a browser.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway's computer, signed in as the account the Gateway runs as, rerun the installer: ./install.sh, or the Gateway installer for Linux, macOS or Windows in the SMTO folder. The installer adds the browser software and the system files it needs; turning on a skill permission doesn't install them.
  2. Wait until no tasks are running on that Gateway, then restart the Gateway, and restart SMTO too if you used ./install.sh. The Gateway only picks up newly installed browser software when it starts.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, and check that its Capabilities now include browser_managed. This confirms the Gateway now reports a working browser.
  4. Start a new task for the browsing work. First check whether anything the earlier task did on websites already happened. Tasks already in progress keep the Gateway abilities they started with, and repeating website actions could do them twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's Capabilities list browser_managed, and a new task can open web pages.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details and the installer's on-screen output to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove the Gateway, its pairing or its browser profiles to start over; repairing in place keeps its sign-ins and settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's Playwright browser backend is unavailable: the playwright package cannot be imported or started, or managed Chromium launch failed with a missing system library or dependency diagnostic.

What this means

  • Browser readiness could not find/load Playwright, or managed Chromium launch returned a recognized missing-library/dependency diagnostic. The latter is a bounded local-launch classification, not a diagnosis from page text. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Browser readiness could not find/load Playwright, or managed Chromium launch returned a recognized missing-library/dependency diagnostic. The latter is a bounded local-launch classification, not a diagnosis from page text.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect browser.status and the local installation/launch phase, distinguishing absent Python backend from missing native libraries.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, as the Gateway's service account, rerun the matching installer (./install.sh, ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1) and require its dependency audit and browser checks to pass. After active work settles, restart the Gateway, confirm browser.status reports ready with the browser_managed capability, and start a new task; inspect the original attempt's receipts before repeating any browser actions.
  • Reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata.
  • From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported installation passes its browser check under the Gateway account and browser.status reports ready.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
